MARKET.head: VINITECH-SIFEL trade show in Bordeaux, 1-3 December 2026, hosts global wine professionals
MARKET.summ: From 1-3 December 2026, Bordeaux will welcome wine professionals from around the world for VINITECH-SIFEL, a leading international trade show dedicated to innovation and solutions for the wine, fruit and vegetable sectors. Bringing together 700 exhibitors, 40,000 professionals from 70 countries and 70,000 m² of exhibition...
takeaways: VINITECH-SIFEL, a Bordeaux trade show for wine, fruit and vegetable sectors, runs 1-3 December 2026.
The show expects 700 exhibitors and 40,000 professionals from 70 countries across 70,000 m² of space.
The International Buyers Program may fund 4-star hotel stays and travel for eligible overseas buyers with investment projects.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA debuts in New York City at Pier 36 in October 2026
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA, organized by Veronafiere with the Italian Trade Agency, holds its first New York City edition at Pier 36 on October 26-27, 2026.
The event moves from Chicago after two years and expects 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels, its largest exhibitor count yet.
Regional collectives from Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Lazio and Sardinia join Asti DOCG, Sicilia DOC and Prosecco DOC, plus 95 wineries from an Italian Trade Agency delegation.

MARKET.head: Global wine shifts from red toward white and sparkling styles, IWSR data shows
MARKET.summ: The global wine industry has been undergoing a significant structural transformation. While declining overall wine consumption has attracted considerable attention, another important trend has emerged beneath the surface: a steady shift in consumer demand from red wine towards white and sparkling wine.
takeaways: IWSR data shows red wine's share of global wine consumption fell from about 52% in 2012 to 43% in 2025.
Over the same period, white wine rose from 31% to 34% and sparkling wine from 8% to 13% of consumption.
Australia's Market Bulletin says the shift matters for its red-led reputation, with Shiraz central to its export position.

MARKET.head: France's 2026 wine harvest set to fall 14% below recent average
MARKET.summ:
This year’s harvest expected to be down 2% on mediocre yield in 2025, when production was lowest in nearly 70 years

France’s wine industry is facing a historic low harvest after the country was hit by a series of summer heatwaves.

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025...
takeaways: France's 2026 harvest is estimated at about 35m hectolitres, down 2% on 2025 and 14% below the 2021-2025 average.
The ministry of agriculture published these estimates, following 2025's lowest French production since 1957 per the OIV.
Champagne production is down by half on last year and the five-year average after an unusually early harvest.

MARKET.head: Australian wine exports to Malaysia, Indonesia and Philippines rise despite declines in West
MARKET.summ: Southeast Asia is an increasingly important region for Australian wine exporters seeking to diversify and build new markets. Population growth, rising household incomes and increasing consumer interest in premium imported beverages are supporting opportunities across the region although market maturity, consumer preferences,...
takeaways: Wine Australia data show Australian wine exports to Malaysia rose 13% in volume and 30% in value to A$55 million in the year to June 2026.
Indonesia's Australian wine exports jumped 88% in volume and 300% in value to A$21 million over the same 12 months.
Australia exported 2.5 million litres worth A$11.5 million to the Philippines, slightly down year on year but above five years ago.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads Liv-ex trade with 33% share as Burgundy follows at 28.5%
MARKET.summ: In this week’s Talking Trade, US buyers maintained their lead of purchasing, with EU buyers behind increasing their purchased value by 140% week-on-week
takeaways: Bordeaux took 33.0% of traded value on Liv-ex this week, ahead of Burgundy at 28.5%.
Domaine de la Romanee-Conti was the top-traded producer, accounting for 10.6% of overall trade.
Champagne fell to 13.9% of traded value from 21.4% the previous week, and US buyers took 47% of Champagne purchases.

MARKET.head: SFI 2026 offers UK vineyards extra payments for cover crops and habitat
MARKET.summ: The second application window for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) is set to open on 22 September, so Hutchinsons head of environmental services, Georgina Wallis, highlights some actions that may be of interest to growers in the viticulture sector. While the SFI is primarily aimed at arable and livestock farms, vines and...
takeaways: The Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) 2026 includes vines and horticultural permanent crops, with several of its 71 actions relevant to vineyards.
Payments could add income for vineyard measures benefiting biodiversity and help meet LEAF Marque v17.0 habitat rules, which require 5% of site area.
Overwinter cover crop (CSAM2) should be sown by late August or early September, but SFI allows up to 12 months to establish a mix.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US wine regions seek new AVA designations, each with distinct terroir
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed new American Viticultural Areas are in early stages, with approval taking several years through the TTB.
Proposed Annapolis-Sea Ranch AVA in Sonoma would cover 26,637 acres with 651 acres of grapes across a dozen vineyards.
Proposed Deschutes River AVA in central Oregon would cover 723,760 acres, the state's first recognized central region.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup covers Southern Glazer's, product drops and industry updates
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. It was a quiet week on the news front, but as we gear up for gifting season, there are a ton of new product drops.
takeaways: California has launched an investigation into distributor Southern Glazer's over a bribery allegation.
Maker's Mark has launched a new product collection ahead of the gifting season.
OpenTable released its 2026 restaurant report, also part of this week's roundup.

CULTURE.head: Adam Wolf discusses Willamette Valley White Pinot Noir Fest on Wine 101
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Meiomi. Celebrate your holiday season to the fullest by bringing, or hosting with, the bottle that makes a lasting impression even after the last drop. From lush aromas of black cherry to warm notes of toasty mocha, Meiomi Pinot Noir is the perfect finish for all of your holiday moments.
takeaways: Adam Wolf of Saffron Fields Vineyards joins host Keith Beavers on the VinePair podcast Wine 101.
The two discuss how the United States celebrates wine in ways unlike any other place on earth.

CULTURE.head: Bartenders say American visitors in Europe are curious, chatty, and still love vodka
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: Giorgio Bargiani of The Connaught Bar in London says American guests are entertaining and show genuine interest in staff and other customers.
Bartenders report American customers often order Martinis made with vodka, and ask for American spirit substitutions and drinks like the Cosmopolitan.
Experienced American travelers increasingly let bartenders guide them, sometimes choosing gin Martinis or local drinks like Westmalle Dubbel.

SCIENCE.head: NMR spectroscopy and chemometrics separate Brazilian tropical wines by vintage and grape cultivar
SCIENCE.summ: Tropical wines have been produced in Northeast of Brazil since 1980’s, between the 8o and 9o S latitude, in a region called Sub-middle São Francisco river Valley
takeaways: Researchers at Federal University of Pernambuco used 1H NMR spectroscopy with PCA and PLS statistics to characterise tropical wines from Northeast Brazil.
The analysis separated wines by vintage and grape cultivar, but failed to discriminate between vintages when white and red wines were combined.
Metabolic compounds were identified as the chemical drivers behind the wine clusters.

SCIENCE.head: Brazilian tropical wines show distinct aroma profiles by colour and harvest month
SCIENCE.summ: Tropical wines have been produced in Thailand, India, Venezuela and mainly in Northeastern Brazil. In Brazil, this activity started twenty-five years ago and has been studied only in the last years. In this Brazilian Area, between 8-9° parallel of the South Hemisphere, it is possible to have two or three harvests per year due...
takeaways: Researchers from Brazilian institutions analysed white and red tropical wines from two 2009 vintages using gas chromatography and multivariate statistics.
Northeast Brazil, at 8-9° South, allows two or three harvests a year thanks to heat, sunlight and irrigation.
Higher alcohols separated wine samples more effectively than volatile esters, and white and red wines had different aromatic compound concentrations.

SCIENCE.head: Brazilian tropical vineyard study measures sunlight reaching Syrah grape clusters
SCIENCE.summ: This work aimed to determine the photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) incidence at the berry level at east (E) and west (W) direction in a Syrah vineyard growing in a tropical semiarid area of Brazil
takeaways: Researchers at Embrapa Tropical Semiarid in Petrolina, Brazil, measured light reaching Syrah berries in a semiarid vineyard during the first half of 2010.
Photosynthetically active radiation at the top of the vineyard was about 40% of incident solar global radiation.
Clusters on east-facing canopy walls received more photosynthetically active light than those on west-facing walls, and leaf removal and shoot trimming changed berry light levels.

SCIENCE.head: Tropical Brazilian red wines keep high polyphenols after a year in bottle
SCIENCE.summ: Young varietal and experimental wines from Vitis vinifera - Petit Verdot, Tempranillo, and Syrah - cultivated in a tropical semiarid region (Northeast Brazil) were evaluated with regard to their phenolic composition and chromatic characteristics during a storage period of 12-month
takeaways: Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah grown in Brazil's semi-arid São Francisco Valley were tracked for 12 months in bottle.
Petit Verdot showed less colour change than wines from temperate climates, per spectrophotometry and HPLC measurements.
Polyphenols fell during storage as expected but stayed above published levels, including anthocyanins in Petit Verdot and trans-resveratrol in Syrah.

SCIENCE.head: Tropical Brazilian, Indian, Thai and Venezuelan wineries now produce quality wine at scale
SCIENCE.summ: A lot of grapes are produced in the tropics, but only a little part is used to winemaking, what represents some million liters of tropical wines produced per year. The present industry of tropical wine production began 30 years ago
takeaways: Commercial tropical wineries now operate in Brazil, India, Thailand and Venezuela, after the industry began about 30 years ago.
Tropical wine output is a few million litres a year, from grapes that are mostly grown for other uses.
Researchers at Embrapa in Brazil say high-quality tropical wine at meaningful volume is likely in the near future.

SCIENCE.head: Undervine heating trials show grapevine fruit set rises or falls by cultivar
SCIENCE.summ: In the 2009/2010 growing season undervine tents (a passive, open system) were used to increase daytime temperature by 3-5 oC over ambient during the growing season. Four grapevine cultivars (Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Semillon and Shiraz) were assessed for reproductive performance under these conditions
takeaways: In 2009/2010, researchers used undervine tents to raise daytime temperatures 3-5°C above ambient across four grape cultivars.
Chardonnay under heat set less fruit, producing fewer berries and lower bunch weights, alongside reduced pollen tube growth.
Semillon and Shiraz under heat set more fruit, with higher berry counts and bunch weights, while Cabernet Franc showed no significant difference.

SCIENCE.head: Rootstock study finds 110 Richter grows most roots under low water
SCIENCE.summ: Grapevine is a landscape forming crop which, due to the quality and taste demanded by consumers, as well as the different agronomical practices, could be vulnerable to global change effects
takeaways: Researchers grew Grenache vines on three rootstocks, 110 Richter, 41-B and 161-49, in rhizotrons with sandy soil under two water regimes.
Root growth peaked in summer during berry growth and ripening, with more roots forming under the higher water dose.
110 Richter produced greater root length than the other two rootstocks, though this did not increase vegetative growth.

SCIENCE.head: Researchers call for multidisciplinary breeding of climate-resilient grapevine rootstocks and scions
SCIENCE.summ: The predicted changes in global climate are of concern to the agriculture of many plant crops including the grapevine. The main environmental parameters to be affected are carbon dioxide atmospheric concentration, temperature, light radiation, water availability and potential evapotranspiration
takeaways: French and Spanish researchers from INRA and several Spanish universities argue climate change threatens viticulture sustainability in several regions.
They say breeding stable-yielding grapevine scions and rootstocks requires ecophysiologists, molecular physiologists and geneticists working together.
The paper also reports tropical wines made from Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah in Northeast Brazil's semiarid São Francisco Valley.

SCIENCE.head: Irrigation water chemistry can strip or supply vineyard soil nutrients
SCIENCE.summ: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. Part Two of a Three-Part Vineyard Mineral Nutrient Management Lab Analysis Series.
takeaways: Nearly pure water such as Sierra Nevada snowmelt strips minerals from soils, especially sandy ones, making them more acidic and less fertile.
Alkaline well water can supply calcium and magnesium, but bicarbonate and carbonate reduce their availability as fertilizer.

SCIENCE.head: Cover crops and mulching boost vineyard soil microbes and resilience, studies find
SCIENCE.summ: Our September newsletter is out. This month: Tasting Climate Change 2026 sessions now available to watch; practical guides on cover crops, weed management and compost teas; fresh research on resilience and economics in regenerative vineyards from France to Sonoma, plus new recognition for ROC and regenerative producers from...
takeaways: Canavera et al. (2026, Environmental Microbiome) found cover crop mulching in a non-irrigated northern Italian vineyard raised microbial diversity and reduced pathogen pressure.
A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards found roller-crimped cover crops improved vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization.
In that Mediterranean study, seasonal climate was the dominant driver of fungal diversity, and grape quality was unaffected.

SCIENCE.head: Hampshire firm Wildflower Co. shortlisted for South Coast tech award
SCIENCE.summ: Hampshire-based biodiversity specialist Wildflower Co. is a finalist in the South Coast Tech and Innovation Awards, in recognition of its groundbreaking use of science and technology to help tackle biodiversity loss and accelerate nature recovery. The pioneering company, which combines more than two decades of scientific...
takeaways: Hampshire biodiversity specialist Wildflower Co. is a finalist in the South Coast Tech and Innovation Awards, Tech for Good category.
The awards ceremony takes place in Southampton on 15 October.
Its Meadowscape Pro system can establish high-quality meadow habitats in three to four months.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A Level Playing Field
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What do we mean by the word “Burgundian”? Used indiscriminately to describe a region that is famously, almost defiantly complex, it’s a term that covers so many appellations, terroirs and styles as to be almost meaningless, especially when it comes to white Burgundy. Are we talking Chablis, the Côte Beaune or the Mâconnais?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin says top Chardonnay is now a level playing field, with world-class examples from Argentina, Australia, Chile, New Zealand, South Africa and the United States.
In a blind tasting organised by Steve Smith MW, 43 tasters scored 24 wines, ten from Pyramid Valley and Smith & Sheth, against 14 from Burgundy.
The 2024 Smith & Sheth Onewa Chardonnay from Hawkes Bay narrowly lost to the 2023 Domaine Guffens-Heynen Saint Véran Clos de Poncetys.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Hazendal, a Stellenbosch wine estate transformed
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hazendal is a historic wine farm in the Bottelary Hills subregion of Stellenbosch that has been transformed. It
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Hazendal, a Bottelary Hills estate in Stellenbosch, replanted its vineyards in 2016 after virus problems reduced production.
Winemaker Kiara Scott Farmer, who arrived in 2024, leads the new era, with 2025 as the first vintage under her direction.
Reviewer scored the 2025 range from 92 to 95 points, with the Chenin Blanc and White Blend rated highest at 95 and 94.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Telling a mountain to move
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delving into the details of change in the DO Montsant wine region of Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: DO Montsant, in Catalunya's Priorat area, has revised its bylaws to add a certification for vi brisat (orange-style) wines.

Montsant's revised bylaws also create a classification for 'minimal intervention' wines, requiring hand-harvesting, organic certification, spontaneous fermentation and no additives except gentle filtration.
The author says the minimal-intervention classification may be the first of its kind in Spain, though the DO has not stated its maximum sulfur dioxide limit.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Most Burgundy Wine Buyers Are Still Shopping Backwards in 2026. Here’s the Strategy Négociants Hope You Never Learn
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Learn the strategy Burgundy wine négociants hope you never discover to find the best winery deals in 2026
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Louis Latour, Louis Jadot, Maison Albert Bichot and Bouchard Père & Fils are named as leading négociant houses dominating Burgundy wine sales worldwide.
It cites Capitain-Gagnerot Corton-Charlemagne and Domaine Jean Féry Puligny-Montrachet as lower-priced alternatives to Coche-Dury and Leflaive Clavoillon.

NEWSLETTERS.head: “Unquestionably Among the Greatest Wines in the World” (Tasting the 2024 Port Vintage)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: You’ll find no shortage of Vintage Port coverage on these virtual pages (something that, as I taste more and more vintages of the stuff, has become a source of amusing vexation as I search for whether or not a VP that I want to feature here has already been reviewed and featured here…). And you’ll […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: The author notes it has become harder to check whether a Vintage Port has already been reviewed on the blog.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 10/11/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting Report: Red and White Wines of Roero
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Recommended Roero Nebbiolo and Arneis wines from my recent tour
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Roero's principal grapes are Nebbiolo and Arneis, both native to Piedmont and rarely grown beyond its borders.
Roero Arneis was nearly extinct until Bruno Giacosa and Alfredo Curado of Vietti resurrected it in the 1970s.
Today Roero has nearly 1,000 hectares of Arneis versus about 360 hectares of Nebbiolo, according to the report.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: A 1350 trade contract between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, held in Florence's State Archives.
A 2024 document unveiled by the Consorzio del Vino Nobile di Montepulciano shows the term 'Vino Nobile' was used by the Jesuits in 1766, predating the previously known 1787 record.
Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano in November 1805 and requested 400 bottles annually, per a letter to Thomas Appleton.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine is out 8th October in the UK and 10th November in the US.
Editor-in-chief David Williams aims for an authoritative but accessible reference, written by acknowledged experts, 28 contributors in total.
The 400-page book is positioned against Oxford Companion to Wine and The World Atlas of Wine, both from Jancis Robinson's team.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Thierry and Louis Germain of Domaine des Roches Neuves
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Two generations from one of Saumur-Champigny’s leading estates on their single-vineyard cuvées and learning to embrace Cabernet Franc’s green side
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Domaine des Roches Neuves, a Saumur-Champigny estate active for 35 years, produces five cuvées parcellaires led by Thierry Germain and his son Louis.
Thierry Germain says single-vineyard wines were rare in Saumur 35 years ago, apart from Clos Rougeard, and he was inspired by Burgundy in the early 1990s.
Louis Germain describes La Marginale, from the Fosse de Chaintres clay soils, as having a velvety, rose-petal texture, while Franc de Pied comes from sandy soils with ungrafted vines.
